style.vernacular: A hill city on red laterite earth: self-built one- and two-storey houses of cement block (parpaing) and brick, often unplastered or painted in cream, ochre and pastel, under rust-red corrugated iron roofs; administrative and hotel buildings of the 1950s to 1980s in brutalist and international style (concrete, glass and steel), with newer glass-and-render commercial blocks. Streets lined with mango, avocado and broadleaf trees.
style.ornament: Brutalist concrete brise-soleil and grid facades on 1960s-80s government blocks; Art Deco and open colonial forms on 1930s buildings; Ewondo and Beti carved wood and bronze statues at museums and churches; pastel stained glass and sacramental murals at Catholic churches; flag masts on esplanades.
